In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the enkephalinergic system in the developing cerebellum is a dynamic one, with the enkephalins being synthesized and transported in the developing cerebella of preweaning rats and being present in the dendrites, dendritic spines, somata and axons of Purkinje and granular neurons.

the immunocytochemical localization of enkepahlin in the cerebellon of the rat during development is associated with both neuronal and glial cells and that this immunoreactive material is associated with the cytoskeleton, endoplasmatic reticulum, mitochondria, and plasma membrane.
enkephalins are present in the developing cerebellum and may participate in the growth and maturation of this region of the brain.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the enkephalin system may play a role in the regulation of the growth and differentiation of cerebellar neurons and glia, and that enkephalins may also be involved in cerebellar synaptic transmission.
enkephalins are synthesized by neurons and glia during the period of rapid growth of the brain, and that they may be associated with the regulation of cell division and differentiation.
enkephalins are present in the cerebellums of 10- and 21-day-old rats, and in the somata, dendrites and dendrite spines of Purkenje cells in 21-day-old animals.
The main takeaway from our work is that
enkephalins are expressed by a wide range of cells during development.
enkephalins are present in the developing cerebellum and that their presence may be important in the regulation of cerebellar cell growth and differentiation.
enkephalins are not confined to neurons, but are also present in developing glial cells.
